chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding

A man has some wealth of orphans with one of his family members, so he hands it over to him. He takes from it dirhams which he needs, and the one who had the wealth of the orphans does not know that he has taken anything from their wealth. Then he becomes affluent after that. Which is better for him: to give it to the one in whose hand it was, or to hand it over to the orphan who has reached maturity? And would it suffice if he hands it over to his companion as a gift and does not inform him that he had taken some wealth of his?

He (peace be upon him) said: Whichever of those he does will suffice for him, when he delivers it to its owner. For this is from the secrets (of the guardian's intention). If it is from his intention to return it to the orphan, if he has reached maturity, in whichever manner he wishes, even if he does not inform him that he had taken something for him; and if he wishes, he can return it to the one in whose hand it was.
And he (peace be upon him) said: If the owner of the wealth is absent, let him hand it over to the one in whose hand it was.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a guardian takes from an orphan's wealth without their knowledge and later repays it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling in the context of *al-sarā'ir* (secrecy), where the guardian may discreetly repay the orphan's wealth to the custodian rather than the orphan directly, provided the intention is to settle the debt. This flexibility highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the guardian's sincere intent (*niyyah*) and practical necessity over rigid formalism, ensuring the orphan's asset is preserved without the need for explicit notification. The ruling underscores the trustworthiness required of guardians managing *mal al-yatīm* (orphan's wealth) under the broader Quranic mandate of careful stewardship.
